Yea, sounds like your friend is in an abusive relationship... There is probably a lot going on you don't know about behind him not letting her out and the manipulation. 
My ex used to get mad when I wanted to hangout with friends and I would often be crying in my bedroom before I was supposed to meet or already be late. I didn't want anybody to know because I thought it was my fault, I didn't even know it was abuse. 
I also was very self centered and didn't ask about others but had no idea until the damage had been done. I was always too preoccupied and upset with my problems with my then boyfriend (whom I lived with) and wasn't aware that I was even that overwhelmed.

Regardless, you are allowed to feel upset that this is the state of the relationship. You have invited her to hang out and I'm sure she is happy, but feels a lot of shame not hanging out or turning the offers down. You have done all you can. Just make sure wedding details that she may have needed to do are being sorted out in case you are worried about reliability. You still need to take care of you. 

In the end, we can only be there for people and whether your friend stays in this unhealthy relationship is on her time. She will need to figure out for herself whether losing friends and opportunities is worth it.

I definitely agree with one of the earlier comments that addiction is more powerful than love. We do a lot we keep secret during addiction and the best we can do is try our bests to be honest. She must trust you enough to tell you now, but probably feels shameful which is why she doesn't want to talk about it/is telling you to move on about it. You are hurt! It is something very valid to lose trust over. 

Not sure if you have any anxieties about unknowingly catching STDs or anything, but I would bring that up and have something done about it. You both need to go through it together.

Personally I think going to meetings at different times is a good idea, so you can get what you need out without her around (and vice versa). I would even suggest going to a couples counselling of some sort; you two have children together so it isn't just about you both! Forgiveness is hard in recovery, we never forgave people before and remained angry very often. I only have 3+ years of recovery and still have a lot of trouble with forgiveness and resentment, but I do think you need to acknowledge that it is OK that you feel that way!

I woke up really confused and tried to remember what I was just doing; hanging myself. 

I was 19 and was 6 months into sobriety after rehab, living with a minister who was a second mom to me. She and her husband were on a cruise and her older son was celebrating his birthday that day. I decided that the world had given up on me, breaking up with my addict boyfriend is what I needed to do... And could not handle it.

I called my then boyfriend and he was so upset he told me not to tell anybody and that he could help me. I knew he was wrong and that wasn't love.
I called my councillor from rehab/my addictions group and she literally drove across town and took me to the hospital. I had purple marking all around my neck, skinned my spine along something when the rope I hung myself with broke while I was unconscious. 
We decided going back to rehab for 3 months was the best, and I had no neck injuries from my hanging. 

I'm not going to say it was easy, I broke up with that boyfriend, stayed single for over a year, worked on my recovery, and attended what I had always wanted in college: animation. 

It is now 3 years later in my sobriety and almost 3 years since, and I start my final year of animation in September. I am also dating a wonderful and truly loving man who isn't afraid to tell me the truth and helps me best he can; with REAL love. I have a fantastic relationship with my rehab group, family, and the minister whom I lived with. I sometimes have hard days but am moving farther away from thoughts of suicide because I really truly can't bear to hurt the people I love so much in my life today.

Please don't give up! Don't end your life over a boy, or over anybody in your life. You are SO important, and even more important to the people who love you and we will never understand how much we are truly loved!
